answer: Two-cluster bridge: a new identity lands only over a bridge built jointly from two clusters sharing no member, and each cluster runs one jetty per epoch, a single ordered landing slot where arrivals are timestamped and diffed against that cluster's history. The bridge counts only when both sides independently lock a bond. Each cluster also holds a nadir, a floor of 12 members with 30-day tenure, before it may bridge anyone, so fresh cheap clusters cannot self-certify. Fielding k sybils needs 2k distinct tenured vouches across disjoint groups, real per-head work no key can parallelize.
